title: Sensory Detail
summary: A told tale lives or dies on whether the listener can SEE the room. This kit listens for the one or two details that put a body in a body, a place in a place.

questions.prompt: Pick one moment in your tale. What did your character SEE, SMELL, HEAR, or TOUCH? Name one of those four. Just one.
Which line gives the listener more to picture?
options: It was a nice day outside.
The sidewalk smelled like wet pavement and bus exhaust, and the sun was already too high.
questions.rationale: Two senses (smell + sight), one moving image, no judgment words ('nice', 'good'). The listener now stands on that sidewalk.

questions.prompt: Listen back. Where did you say 'really' or 'super' or 'so' as a stand-in for a real detail? Pick one. Replace it with the actual thing.
Rewrite this line so the listener can stand inside the moment: 'It was super hot at the bus stop.' Use one sense, not three.

castCameos.line: Setup steady. You gave the room one detail to settle into before you moved. That's pacing.
Specificity pulled me forward again. The sidewalk-and-bus-exhaust line — my body tipped.
Hold this detail. When the turn comes, you can rotate it.
If you said this detail twice — once at the open, once at the close — it would carry more weight the second time.
